featured.title: Iran Threatens New Gulf Exclusion Zone as Oil Prices Rise
featured.content: Iran says it plans to establish a new maritime exclusion zone in the Persian Gulf and has warned of further missile action against US forces. The announcement comes as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely reduced. Brent crude rose to around $97.34 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate reached about $92.63 as traders priced in the possibility of prolonged disruption to Gulf energy supplies.

articles.title: Iran announces planned Gulf maritime exclusion zone
articles.content: Iran has announced plans to establish a new maritime exclusion zone in the Persian Gulf and says vessels entering the defined area could face sanctions. Tehran's announcement follows recent exchanges with US forces, including Iranian missile attacks on US warships. The move adds another layer of uncertainty around commercial shipping and energy supplies.
articles.imageQuery: Iran Persian Gulf maritime exclusion zone

articles.title: Hormuz shipping disruption keeps global energy markets on edge
articles.content: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely reduced. Reuters reports that only about seven commodity vessels were recorded crossing the waterway on Monday, compared with eight the previous day. The decline is adding pressure to global energy markets and raising concerns about transport and consumer costs.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz oil tanker shipping

articles.title: Brent crude climbs above $97
articles.content: Brent crude rose to around $97.34 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate reached about $92.63 as traders assessed the possibility of prolonged disruption to Gulf energy supplies. Analysts expect elevated prices to remain a risk if shipping disruptions continue.

articles.title: Russian missiles strike Kyiv after US peace envoys leave
articles.content: Russia launched a renewed ballistic-missile attack on Kyiv early Tuesday shortly after US peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff departed the Ukrainian capital. Ukrainian officials said six people were injured, residential buildings were damaged and fires broke out. Poland also activated military aviation measures to protect its airspace.

articles.title: Peace talks continue despite renewed attacks
articles.content: The Kyiv attack came after US representatives held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. Earlier discussions also took place in Moscow with Russian officials. No peace agreement has been reached, and the latest missile attack highlights the difficulty of making diplomatic progress while fighting continues.
articles.imageQuery: Ukraine peace talks Zelenskiy US envoys

articles.title: Dangote Refinery announces $14.3 billion expansion
articles.content: Dangote Refinery has announced a $14.3 billion expansion plan that would increase capacity from around 700,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029. The announcement was made as the company signed documents for its planned IPO.

articles.title: Dangote IPO targets ₦2.15 trillion
articles.content: The proposed Dangote Refinery IPO is expected to raise about ₦2.15 trillion, equivalent to approximately $1.63 billion. The offer is scheduled to run from September 14 to October 13, with trading potentially beginning later in November, subject to the final process.
articles.imageQuery: Dangote Refinery IPO Nigeria stock market

articles.title: Dangote Refinery reports major turnaround in first-half profit
articles.content: Dangote Refinery's IPO prospectus shows the company made approximately $1.82 billion in profit during the first half of 2026, compared with a $476 million loss during the same period of 2025. The figures underline the refinery's growing importance to Nigeria's energy and capital markets.

articles.title: Nigeria could double energy investment within five years
articles.content: International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol says Nigeria could potentially double investment in its energy sector within five years. He highlighted opportunities across oil, gas and renewable energy as Nigeria seeks greater investment and stronger energy production.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria energy investment oil gas renewable

articles.title: Uber ends 12-year operation in Nigeria
articles.content: Uber has ended its ride-hailing operations in Nigeria after 12 years. The company stopped offering rides in the country on September 2. The exit marks a significant change in Nigeria's competitive ride-hailing market, which faces high fuel costs, inflation and currency pressures.

articles.title: Japanese yen reaches seven-month high
articles.content: The Japanese yen surged to a seven-month high against the US dollar, reaching 152.89 before settling around 153.32. The currency has gained roughly 4.5% since the previous week as traders increase bets on a Bank of Japan interest-rate hike and unwind positions that had favoured a weaker yen.
articles.imageQuery: Japanese yen currency Tokyo financial markets

articles.title: Asian markets mixed as geopolitical risks grow
articles.content: Asian stocks were mixed on Tuesday as investors assessed rising Middle East tensions and changing interest-rate expectations. Japan's Nikkei edged higher, South Korea's KOSPI gained, while Australian shares declined. Oil prices continued to rise as Iran warned of possible retaliation against US energy infrastructure.
articles.imageQuery: Asian stock market trading Tokyo Seoul

articles.title: EU announces €200 million investment partnership with Greenland
articles.content: The European Union has announced a €200 million partnership with Greenland covering areas including digital connectivity, sustainable mining, energy, tourism, education, fisheries and housing. The move comes amid growing geopolitical interest in the Arctic and renewed US pressure over Greenland.

articles.title: Gaza rubble clearance raises evidence concerns
articles.content: UN expert Francesca Albanese has warned that clearing rubble in Gaza could destroy evidence potentially relevant to investigations into alleged serious violations of international law and could also complicate the recovery and identification of human remains. Palestinian medical authorities continue to report casualties from Israeli strikes.

articles.title: Nigeria's economic picture remains mixed
articles.content: Nigeria recorded 4.43% year-on-year GDP growth in the second quarter of 2026, according to official data. At the same time, the country continues to face pressure from high living costs and infrastructure challenges. The expansion of Dangote Refinery and increased energy investment could become important factors in the country's economic outlook.

articles.title: Global markets watch inflation and interest-rate decisions
articles.content: Investors are closely monitoring oil prices, bond yields and inflation expectations as geopolitical tensions increase energy costs. Upcoming US inflation data and expectations for central-bank decisions are likely to influence global financial markets.

morningSummary: Good morning. Tuesday begins with heightened geopolitical and economic uncertainty. Iran is threatening a new maritime exclusion zone in the Persian Gulf, oil has climbed above $97 a barrel and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted. Russia has also launched a fresh missile attack on Kyiv following US peace talks. In Nigeria, Dangote Refinery has announced a $14.3 billion expansion alongside its historic IPO, while Uber's exit marks another major change in the country's business landscape.
bigQuestion: With oil prices rising because of international conflict, can Nigeria turn its growing energy capacity into real economic relief for ordinary citizens?
